C-VNEXT-RUNTIME-TRUTH-RECONCILIATION-202.Summary: Establish an evidence-backed current-state baseline before further vNext implementation by reconciling runtime support, trusted-computing-base ownership, GRACE linkage, verification routing, readiness language, and the composite integration delta.
C-VNEXT-RUNTIME-TRUTH-RECONCILIATION-202.Problem: The Astra audit found that current architecture labels overstate several real paths: CEF advertises operations it returns as Unsupported, reference proving slices are sometimes read as real-engine evidence, all ten GRACE modules lack linked non-test governed files, and existing verification commands do not always point clearly to their evidence. Without a corrected baseline, later agents can optimize against false abstractions and silently enlarge the trusted boundary.

Goals.Goal: Publish a per-backend operation support matrix that distinguishes contract, reference, CEF, native-process, WASM, and future engine profiles.
Publish a TCB and effective-resource map covering kernel, mandatory brokers, engine process, updater and recovery launcher, feature host, storage, UI security surfaces, OS, and third-party runtimes.
Reconcile current GRACE graph and verification linkage to real implementation and test files using repository-approved semantic markup.
Align roadmap, ADR, graph, verification, and CI claims with scaffolded, wired, and verified evidence states.
Record the current active search bundle and the P0 through P3 integration delta without changing their approved contracts.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
This change is current-state reconciliation. It must not change production behavior, public runtime contracts, security policy, or persisted schemas.
The approved C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 spec and plan are immutable and outside observed write scope.
The unrelated untracked scripts/Maintain-CargoCache.ps1 file is external drift and must remain untouched.
Reference, model, fixture, local, hosted, device, and manual evidence must remain separately labelled.
Do not manufacture fine-grained graph modules before separate ownership and verification exist.
Do not mark unsupported CEF operations as available or treat process cleanup as an OS security sandbox.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Implementing effect fences, package activation, feature sandboxing, UI composition, or brokered I/O.
Merging the composite integration branch into master.
Executing, modifying, applying, or archiving the active browser-search change.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A versioned operation-support matrix names every currently declared browser operation and reports Reference, CEF, and other runtime support as Implemented, Unsupported, Degraded, or NotPresent with source anchors.
A versioned TCB/resource map identifies which component owns identity, policy, authorization, effect commit, credentials, network egress, engine state, UI trust indicators, updates, and recovery.

Every current graph module links to at least one real non-test implementation owner through valid GRACE semantic markup, or is explicitly narrowed through an approved graph delta rather than left as an unexplained blocker.
Every current verification entry has commands that clearly address its declared test files or documents, with deliberate exceptions documented.
grace status reports no unexplained missing-implementation linkage blockers introduced or preserved by this reconciliation.
Roadmap and ADR status language distinguishes contract/model-tested, wired, and verified and does not promote ReferenceBrowserBackend evidence to real CEF evidence.
The active C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 spec and plan remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
The integration delta remains decomposed into P0 through P3 with explicit TCB, capability, engine-profile, evidence, and rollback review requirements.
A completion packet reports exact files changed, current dirty-tree coexistence, commands, unresolved evidence gaps, and no-runtime-delta confirmation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: A machine-readable current-state report has zero unexplained module-linkage blockers, the support and TCB maps cite real files, architecture guards remain green, and no production behavior changed.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current ten GRACE blockers primarily reflect absent file-local semantic linkage rather than absent Rust implementation; the plan must verify this per module.
Existing coarse module ownership remains sufficient for reconciliation; any module split requires an explicit target graph delta in the later approved plan.
The audit snapshot and integration ledger are valid decision inputs but do not replace fresh repository inspection during planning.
